w1031-01-cold-heart.vo: Lift him too roughly, and this hypothermia rescue could stop his heart. He went through the ice, and he's been in that freezing lake WAY too long. A heart this cold gets twitchy, so ONE hard jolt can tip it into ventricular fibrillation. That's when the heart stops pumping. It just quivers. [curious] And the scary part? A fast, rough pull, the kind anyone would try, could be that jolt. [warmly] So instead, the rescuers keep him flat and slide him slowly across the ice. They handle him like he's made of glass. And handled that gently... his cold heart keeps beating, slow but steady, all the way to shore.
